decisive_moments.reason: Pro usefully narrowed the proposal to a replay contract with exact replay where feasible and explicit nondeterministic boundaries, but this materially weakened the original claim of deterministic replay as the standard requirement.

Con identified the unresolved operational standard: the debate never established objective criteria for when a nondeterministic boundary is sufficiently explicit or testable, nor how to avoid false assurance from replay-adjacent evidence.

Con clearly distinguished the defensible policy—risk-proportional provenance, invariants, rollback, and replay where meaningful—from the broader default requirement. This better addressed privacy, cost, capability, and developer-freedom tradeoffs.

flags.quote: Deterministic replay—or an explicit, testable substitute—should therefore be the standard production requirement.
Users bear the downside of irreproducible actions; developers control architecture and can choose compliant implementations.
The pro side has conceded the decisive point
